title: Amazon opens fulfillment center, with 2nd ready soon
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is expanding its operations in Central Ohio with the opening of a new fulfillment center. This facility is being developed by Duke Realty Corp. in Obetz. This move signals a widening of Amazon's network in the region.

title: Amazon passes Exxon to become 4th most valuable company in the U.S.
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has surpassed Exxon Mobil Corp. to become the fourth-largest U.S. company by market capitalization, with Exxon falling to sixth place behind Facebook Inc. This shift places an all-technology top five among U.S. companies. Amazon's rise follows strong second-quarter results, during which it climbed three spots, also overtaking Berkshire Hathaway Inc.

title: You Can Buy Amazon Kindles at Target Again
summary: Target is reintroducing Amazon's Kindle e-readers, Fire tablets, and Fire TV devices to its website immediately and to stores in October, four years after removing them. This decision comes despite previous concerns about Amazon drawing customers away, as a survey shows many Target customers already have Amazon Prime memberships. The retailer aims to offer convenience and value to its customers, recognizing their existing engagement with Amazon's ecosystem.

title: Apple Says It Has Fixed Gender Pay Gap For U.S. Employees
summary: Apple has announced that it has closed the gender wage gap for its employees in the United States, with women and underrepresented minorities earning one dollar for every dollar male and white employees earn, respectively. The company is now analyzing its global workforce to address any existing pay disparities worldwide. This achievement aligns with similar announcements from Facebook and Amazon and reflects Apple's focus on hiring more women and diverse candidates, with a slight shift in its workforce composition and over half of new hires being minorities.

title: Amazon Prime Air Takes Off
summary: Amazon officially unveiled its Prime Air cargo service, showcasing its first Boeing 767-300 cargo plane. The company plans to grow its dedicated fleet to 40 planes, leased from Air Transport Services Group Inc. and Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings Inc., to handle up to 30% of its shipping volume by 2018. This move is expected to generate significant cost savings for Amazon and poses a challenge to established carriers like UPS and FedEx.

title: Google executive speaks at Purdue summer commencement
summary: Jim Miller, a Purdue alumnus and Google's vice president of operations, delivered the keynote address at Purdue University's summer commencement. The ceremony saw approximately 1,403 students eligible for degrees. Miller shared how his Purdue education shaped his successful career at major companies like Google, Amazon, Cisco, IBM, Intel, and Teledesic.

title: 9 things stores don't want you to know
summary: This article reveals nine strategies stores use to encourage consumers to spend more money, often under the guise of deals or convenience. It highlights tactics such as inflated "sales," free shipping minimums, misleading bulk bargains, BOGO deals, and psychological tricks used in dressing rooms and store layouts. The piece advises consumers on how to navigate these retail ploys to save money, like asking for price matches and understanding store credit card pitfalls.

title: Amazon’s (AMZN) Offices in Japan Raided; Will Stock Be Affected?
summary: Amazon's Japan office was raided by the Japan Fair Trade Commission on suspicion of unfairly forcing retailers to favor its website over rivals. Despite this, Amazon's stock remains an attractive option for investors, with strong growth and financial performance, and analysts giving it a "buy" rating. The incident is not expected to significantly affect the company's overall operations or stock value.

title: Wal-Mart to Acquire Jet.com for $3.3 Billion to Fight Amazon
summary: Wal-Mart Stores Inc. has agreed to acquire e-commerce startup Jet.com Inc. for approximately $3.3 billion, in a significant move to challenge Amazon.com Inc. Founder Marc Lore will take charge of Wal-Mart's combined online operations. The deal includes $3 billion in cash and $300 million in shares, representing Wal-Mart's largest-ever acquisition in the U.S.

title: China's JD.com revenue meets expectations as slowdown set to continue
summary: JD.com Inc. reported second-quarter revenue that met company forecasts, despite a continued decline in growth rate. The company anticipates an even sharper decline in growth for the third quarter, raising concerns about saturation in China's e-commerce sector. Despite net losses, JD.com saw a 47 percent increase in merchandise transactions and updated its share repurchase program.

title: Macy's to close 100 stores, tweak e-commerce experiences as retail landscape continues major shift
summary: Macy's Inc. announced it would close 100 stores across the U.S. to adapt to the changing retail landscape, focusing on better-performing physical stores, online shopping, and mobile apps. The company plans to invest in technology to improve digital properties and in-store experiences, aiming to offset an expected $1 billion sales loss from the closures through expense savings. This strategic shift comes as Macy's and other traditional retailers like Nordstrom and Walmart (with its acquisition of Jet.com) are grappling with the dominance of e-commerce giants like Amazon.

title: How Amazon Destroys Hundreds of Thousand of Jobs
summary: This article discusses how the rise of Amazon and e-commerce is leading to significant job losses at traditional brick-and-mortar retailers. Companies like Macy's, Gap, and Sears are closing numerous stores and laying off thousands of employees as they struggle to compete with Amazon's efficiency and scale. The piece highlights that while these layoffs have started, they are far from over, with the critical holiday shopping season potentially worsening the situation for many retailers.

title: Ronald D. Boire Steps Down as Chief of Barnes & Noble (Published 2016)
summary: Ronald D. Boire, CEO of Barnes & Noble, is leaving the company after less than a year due to a "not a good fit" determination by the board. This marks the third CEO departure in three years for the struggling bookstore chain. The company's founder, Leonard Riggio, will postpone his retirement to lead until a successor is found.

title: Billionaire Steve Cohen Poured Money Into Amazon, Tesoro, Others in Q2
summary: This article details how billionaire hedge fund manager Steve Cohen's Point72 Asset Management significantly increased its holdings in several companies during Q2 2016, including Amazon.com, Inc. and KAR Auction Services Inc. It highlights the value and performance of these investments, providing insights into Cohen's investment strategy despite being barred from managing money for outside investors until 2018. The piece emphasizes the importance of following institutional investor moves, especially for small-cap stocks.

title: Lyft Is Said to Seek a Buyer, Without Success (Published 2016)
summary: Lyft, the second-largest ride-hailing company in the U.S., has reportedly sought a buyer but ultimately failed to secure a deal, despite holding talks with several major companies including General Motors, Apple, and Google. The company remains independent with a $1.4 billion cash reserve, highlighting the capital-intensive and challenging nature of the ride-hailing market. Though G.M. was considered the most serious suitor, no written offer was ever made.

title: Retailers zero in on college market
summary: Retailers like Target, Amazon, Wal-Mart, and Best Buy are increasingly focusing on college campuses to tap into a younger consumer base, expanding their operations with small, convenient stores and pick-up locations. This strategy aims not only to capture a niche market but also to introduce their brands to young consumers who are still forming their preferences. The college market is described as an "emerging battleground" where students often price-check between retailers like Target and Amazon.

title: Baozun Inc. launches warehousing, logistics solutions subsidiary
summary: Baozun Inc., a Chinese e-commerce solutions provider, has launched Baotong E-logistics, a wholly-owned warehousing and logistics subsidiary. This new entity aims to strengthen Baozun's warehousing and fulfillment services and expand its reach to a larger number of brand partners, particularly as e-commerce grows in China. Baotong will manage Baozun's seven distribution centers and plans to open its first premium warehouse, the Baotong Cube, next month.

title: Dollar General, Dollar Tree tumble as competition heats up
summary: Dollar General and Dollar Tree both reported weaker-than-expected Q2 2016 sales and earnings, causing their shares to tumble. The companies cited increased competition, food stamp declines, and a challenging retail environment as factors impacting their performance. Despite past resilience during economic downturns, the dollar store retailers are now facing pressure from competitors like Walmart and Amazon as consumers' willingness to spend increases.

title: Domino’s Is One Step Closer to Delivering Pizzas by Drone
summary: Domino's Pizza Enterprises conducted a drone delivery demonstration in Auckland, New Zealand, aiming to be the first company to launch regular drone delivery services. Partnering with Flirtey, Domino's expects trial store-to-door deliveries to begin later this year, leveraging New Zealand's favorable drone regulations. The company believes drone delivery will enhance efficiency and reach more customers, building on its recent technological investments and success.

title: This City Is Getting Amazon’s Latest Physical Bookstore
summary: Amazon is expanding its brick-and-mortar bookstore presence with a new location planned for Chicago's Lakeview neighborhood. This will be Amazon's fourth physical bookstore, which leverage online data like customer ratings and sales totals to curate their inventory. The strategy aims to cater to continued interest in paper books and provide a physical space for customers to experience Amazon's devices.

title: G.E., the 124-Year-Old Software Start-Up (Published 2016)
summary: General Electric is undergoing a major transformation to become a top software company by 2020, investing heavily in its GE Digital division and developing an industrial operating system called Predix. This initiative aims to monetize the vast amounts of data generated by its industrial machinery, moving beyond traditional hardware sales to offering "business outcomes" and facing new competition from tech giants. The company is also striving to change its century-old engineering culture to embrace Silicon Valley's agile development practices.
